The plaintiff Sree Sree Ram Krishna Dev Bigraha Asram represented by its Shebait instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 611 of 1978 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail, originally praying for a permanent injunction against the defendants 1-4. Subsequently on the prayer of the plaintiff, the suit was amended as one for a declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction, in respect of the suit land comprising 3.46 decimals of land as described in the schedule of the plaint and in the alternative with a prayer for recovery of khas possession of the suit-land if the plaintiff was found out of possession of the suit land. The plaintiff further prayed for a declaration that the sale held in certificate case Nos. 201-A of 1969-70 and 207 of 1969-70 was illegal, fraudulent, and null and void. 

 "The learned Munsif further held that the defendant Nos. 1-3 having at least obtained a symbolical possession of the suit land the present suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and permanent injunction was not maintainable. But we find from the record that the plaintiff also made an alternative prayer for recovery of khas possession of the suit-land, if he was-found dispossessed thereof. Such prayer was quite maintainable in the given facts and circumstances of the case. But the learned Munsif over-looked the said relief prayer by the plaintiff and held the suit was not maintainable without prayer for such a relief." 

 17. Now, keeping in view the above settlement principles in deciding issues in a suit particularly any issue of law independently, when the instant case is considered, it is found that the suit, was dismissed by the trial Court holding that the same was not maintainable while disposing of an application for temporary injunction. On scrutiny of the records, the learned Advocate for the appellant could not show that there was any date fixed by the trial Court for framing any issue in the suit. Even it is not found from the order-sheet of the suit that any written statement was then filed by the defendants. It rather transpires that after filing of the suit, the plaintiff at one filed an application for temporary injunction and only in that connection the learned Munsif, now Assistant Judge held that the suit was not maintainable mainly on the ground thin some proceeding in connection with the setting aside of the auction sale in question was still pending and further there was no prayer for recovery of khas possession as because the auction purchaser defendant Nos. 1-3 took symbolical possession of the suit land. Now, question is whether in such a stage of the suit when issues were not settled and even the written statement from the side of the defendants was not filed, passing of such order of dismissal of the suit on the ground of its maintainability without giving opportunity to the parties to lead any evidence was justified at all, although the provisions of Order 14 rule (2) and Order 15 rule (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure under certain circumstances allow independent disposal of any issue of law after filing of the written statement and framing of issues in the suit? From the judgment of the lower appellate Court, it appears that the learned Subordinate Judge examined the impugned judgment of the trial Court on various considerations and ultimately he found that even on the question of maintainability of the suit so many other incidental issues are involved and without sufficient evidence to be brought on record by the parties the same cannot be decided properly in accordance with the law and hence he has found illegality in the impugned decision of the trial Court and set aside the same and sent back the suit on remand to the trial Court for regular trial and decision in accordance with law in the light of his observation after giving an opportunity to the plaintiff to amend the schedule of the land in the plaint and also allowing the parties to lead further evidence if any in support of their respective cases for the ends of justice.
